$comment: An entry needs a reason a reviewer can check and a reviewBy date.
The build fails if the acceptance expires, if the advisory or package identity stops
matching, if the accepted package version changes without review, or if the affected
functionality becomes reachable in our own source. Removing the vulnerable dependency
also requires removing its entry: a stale acknowledgement fails the build too.

acknowledged.reason: No patched release exists: GitHub lists braces <=3.0.3 as affected with no first patched version, and 3.0.3 is the latest published version, so there is nothing to upgrade or override to. braces reaches the tree only through tailwindcss@3 (chokidar and micromatch), which expands glob patterns from our own tailwind.config content paths at build time. The audit labels it runtime only because tailwindcss-animate (a Tailwind plugin in dependencies) declares tailwindcss as a peer; no braces, micromatch or chokidar code is in the built bundle a browser loads. The DoS needs an attacker-controlled, deeply nested brace pattern, and the only patterns passed are fixed strings in our repository. Re-review when braces publishes a fix or by the date below.

reachability.description: Fails if our own source starts importing braces or the glob libraries that wrap it, which would let untrusted patterns reach it.
